summary: AGRITECH is a lightweight web app that helps Ivorian farmers choose the right crop, in the right place, at the right time. Côte d'Ivoire has several agro-ecological zones — forest, savanna, coastal, mountain — each with its own soil, seasons, and suitable crops. Yet many farmers still decide by habit, without localized guidance, which leads to wrong crops, bad timing, and lost harvests — a problem made worse by climate change. AGRITECH solves this in three simple steps: the user clicks their zone on an interactive map, sees a month-by-month calendar of rainy and dry seasons, and gets a list of recommended crops with a compatibility score (green = ideal, orange = possible, brown = risky). Plots and preferences are saved locally, so the app works fully offline on any phone, with no installation and no internet needed. It is built first for small and medium-sized farmers, but also serves agricultural advisors, cooperatives, NGOs, and students. The goal is simple: fewer losses, better yields, and safer incomes.
details:
AGRITECH helps farmers and agricultural advisors in Côte d’Ivoire answer one question: which crop should I plant, where, and when? (Challenge: Field Shift — Adapting Farms with NASA Data.)

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS
The user picks a region, a crop (or all crops) and a period, or clicks anywhere on an interactive map of the country. AGRITECH ranks the best-suited crops out of 38, with a score out of 99 and a plain-language explanation (temperature, rainfall, soil pH, soil texture). It also shows the area’s season calendar (two rainy seasons in the south, one in the north), the best sowing and harvest months, a climate stress gauge, a sowing alert and a risk view (low rainfall plus heat). NASA POWER (Daily and Monthly APIs, parameters T2M and PRECTOTCORR) provides live 30-day conditions for a clicked point and 12-month averages per region, and these feed the score. If the API cannot be reached, the app falls back to clearly labelled indicative values.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Choosing the wrong crop or the wrong month can cost a farmer a whole season. AGRITECH is meant to turn NASA climate data into simple, actionable guidance for people who are not data experts, and to help advisors support farmers with a printable sheet. We aim to reduce planting mistakes and help farms adapt to a more variable climate.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

  • HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript in a single lightweight file, with an interactive SVG map and no external library.
  • NASA POWER API as the live data source.
  • Real administrative boundaries from GADM (31 regions plus the districts of Abidjan and Yamoussoukro), processed with Python.
  • Two Google Fonts (Bricolage Grotesque and Atkinson Hyperlegible).
  • Claude (Anthropic) assisted us in writing the interface code. No AI runs inside the application: the ranking is rule-based.
  • Our team’s wider project also includes a backend (Bun, TypeScript, Elysia) and a React frontend, which this prototype is not yet connected to.
  • No special hardware: it runs in any modern browser, including on phones.

WHAT IS CREATIVE
Planning is built around the calendar: the user chooses the month and sees what to sow and harvest. Real regional boundaries make the map clickable down to each region, and three map views (best crop by family, score for one crop, risk zones) make the data easy to read at a glance. A guided demo explains each result step by step.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

  • Accessibility: French and English, keyboard navigation, high contrast, light and dark themes.
  • Low-connectivity use: one small file with a fallback when the data service is unavailable.
  • Privacy: no accounts, and no personal data is sent anywhere.
  • Regional climate differences between the north and south.
  • Transparency about limits: soil data, crop ranges and calendars are indicative in this prototype. The tool measures suitability, not profitability, because it has no price or yield data yet.
